slides.title: Coroutines and the Event Loop
slides.prompt: Coroutines are functions declared with `async def`. Calling a coroutine doesn't execute it immediately; it returns a coroutine object. `asyncio.run()` manages the event loop lifecycle and executes the entry-point coroutine.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio

async def main():
    print("Hello")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("World")

asyncio.run(main())
